subject: Aperture — competitive match and migration economics
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aperture — initial briefing (competitive match + migration ask)

Team — quick briefing on Aperture Health (they're an EMR-adjacent analytics buyer). Liam (procurement lead) and their legal (Sarah) have asked for: competitor pricing evidence, a migration credit, and a concrete go-live timing to justify a multi-year commitment. Key constraints: procurement expects parity on list price + a migration buffer; engineering cares about KV cache compatibility and a 6-week pilot window.

Questions for the thread:
- How far can we push on headline discount without eroding margin?
- Can we commit to an onboarding credit tied to milestones (pilot completion + production ramp)?
- Do we have SOC2 and egress guarantees handy for Sarah/legal?

My suggested play: a conditional competitive match up to 18% year‑one discount + a fixed one-time migration credit (not to exceed $150k) if they sign MSA within two weeks of this offer. That keeps the headline credible but preserves negotiating room for an expanded dedicated capacity contract.

Please reply with:
- Jordan: draft outbound (I can review)
- Neha: high-level economics (quick P&L delta)
- Kimberly: legal/finance constraints for a $150k credit and invoice timing

— Grace
Senior Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperturehealth.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood follow-up — competitive match and migration plan

Hi Liam & Sarah — great to meet briefly on Monday. Following up with a concrete starting point so your procurement queue has something to work with. We appreciate you sharing the competitor numbers; to make progress we typically need: list price comparison, term length, and any onboarding subsidies.

High-level preliminary offer (subject to legal/finance sign-off):
- Match competitor list price for year 1 (up to 18% off our standard list)
- One-time migration credit up to $150,000 tied to documented milestones: (1) pilot go/no-go; (2) production cutover within 90 days of pilot finish
- 60-day pilot at no additional runtime cost for the pilot cluster (standard support included)

Attached: draft migration_estimate.xlsx (high level takeoff) and a short playbook for takeover scenarios. If this looks directionally right, can you send the procurement worksheet with the competitor line items and expected start dates? That will let us convert this into a written offer and a DocuSign MSA link.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: migration_estimate.xlsx, takeover_playbook.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperturehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@aperturehealth.com>, procurement@aperturehealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up — competitive match and migration plan

Jordan — thanks. Quick answers and a couple attachments from our side: I've attached our procurement worksheet that shows current vendor pricing and the MSA summary our legal prefers. Highlights:
- Current vendor effective price (avg utilization): $0.011/token equivalent (we can send raw invoices if useful)
- They're offering a two‑quarter volume guarantee in exchange for a 15% discount; in practice we've been at ~85% of guaranteed usage
- Procurement is focused on invoice schedule and liability carveouts for data access during migration

We would be open to your proposed migration credit. Two asks from legal:
1) SOC 2 Type II report (we need to validate controls)
2) Clear language on log retention and audit access during the pilot period

Sending procurement worksheet as: Aperture_procurement_workbook.xlsx. Can we get a written offer that includes: proposed invoice schedule, credit timing (when will the $150k be applied), and a short checklist of what constitutes 'pilot completion'?

— Liam
Director, Strategic Procurement
Aperture Health
Attachments: Aperture_procurement_workbook.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Aperture competitive math (internal)

Looping in quick economics. Using the procurement worksheet Liam shared, rough delta:
- If we match effective price (approx 15% headline) and provide $150k migration credit amortized over 12 months, incremental gross margin impact is ~6–8% in year 1 depending on seat growth assumptions.
- If we tie the credit to milestones (50% at pilot signoff, 50% at production cutover), cash flow impact is manageable and reduces churn risk.

Recommendation: approve up to 18% headline match but require 12‑month minimum commitment and a pilot acceptance checklist that includes: KV cache validation, latency SLA baseline (p95 < 220ms), and a data access/egress plan.

Also noted: Sarah's SOC2 request is standard — attach the redacted SOC2 and a short evidence packet. Kimberly, finance/legal will we be able to get sign-off on the milestone schedule below?

— Neha
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aperturehealth.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Written offer & pilot acceptance criteria (redwood)

Liam / Sarah — per our internal review, attaching a written offer and pilot acceptance checklist. Executive summary below: 
- Headline: up to 18% discount off Redwood list for year 1 if MSA executed by 2026-11-24
- Migration credit: $150,000 one-time credit, applied to invoice after production cutover (split: 50% after pilot acceptance, 50% post-production cutover)
- Pilot: 60-day technical pilot; acceptance criteria: KV cache parity test, p95 latency < 220ms on representative workload, replication/egress checklist completed
- Invoice schedule: quarterly in arrears; migration credit applied as a credit memo against the first post-cutover invoice

I'm sharing a DocuSign link for the draft MSA once you confirm the commercial terms: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ABCDEF-123456

Attachments: Aperture_MA.pdf (MSA draft), migration_estimate.xlsx (cost takeoff).

Please flag any legal items that won't work for you and we'll loop Kimberly/our legal ops in to resolve.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Aperture — approval to proceed with conditional offer

All — confirming legal & finance alignment on the proposed structure. Approvals and constraints: 
- Legal: acceptable to proceed with the MSA redline as long as we add the redacted SOC2 Type II and a 30-day audit access window for the pilot period. We'll push back on any open-ended indemnity language.
- Finance: can approve a $150k migration credit with the milestone split (50/50) and quarterly invoicing. We'll require Aperture to sign an addendum acknowledging the credit amortization to avoid future disputes.

Next steps: Jordan, send the DocuSign MSA link to Liam and Sarah with the attachments and copy finance (finance.ops@redwoodinference.com). Grace, please confirm if we want to extend the headline cap to 18% (vs 15%) — my recommendation: stick to 18% cap but make it conditional on a 12-month minimum and signature by 2026-11-24. I attached a short offer letter for Aperture that mirrors the MSA (Aperture_written_offer.pdf).

— Kimberly
Director, Contracts & Billing
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Aperture_written_offer.pdf
